title: Cost Shepherd: adaptive region slot balancer with spot/on-demand and GPU-class budget caps
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
We need a routing component that enforces per-tenant budget caps while maximizing SLO attainment. Current cost-aware routing favors spot and cheaper regions but lacks finesse for GPU-class objectives (e.g., prefer A100 for latency-critical requests, allow T4/RTX for low-priority) and doesn't gracefully degrade when per-tenant budget windows are exhausted. This ticket designs and implements the "Cost Shepherd": an adaptive region slot balancer that combines predictive spot-eviction hedging, GPU-type preference profiles, and soft/hard budget caps with transparent fallbacks to model variants and regional tiers.

Goals:
- Enforce tenant budget windows (hourly/daily) with soft throttles and hard caps while minimizing SLO violations.
- Choose instance class (GPU family) based on request priority, model variant compatibility, and remaining budget headroom.
- Prefer spot/spot-blend by default but automatically shift to on-demand when predicted eviction risk + SLO cost exceed budget tradeoff.
- Allow automatic fallback to cheaper model variants (quantized/2x smaller) when budget pressure is high.
- Provide observability: per-request decisions recorded with cost delta, chosen GPU class, eviction-risk score, and budget attribution.

Design summary:
1) Budget accounting:
- Maintain a rolling budget window (configurable: 1h / 6h / 24h) per tenant. Each request reserves an estimated token-cost budget based on model, sequence length percentiles and chosen GPU family multiplier. Reservations can be committed or released based on actual usage.
- Soft cap: when usage > soft_threshold (e.g., 80%), start applying graded de-prioritization (reduce burst slots, prefer cheaper GPU types, enable cheaper model variants).
- Hard cap: reject or queue non-critical requests and immediately shift critical requests to on-demand or lower-cost variants depending on policy.

2) GPU-class selection heuristics:
- Each model advertises a GPU affinity score vector (A100:0.9, H100:0.95, A10G:0.6, T4:0.3) and a quantization compatibility flag.
- Request has priority tier: P0 (latency-SLO), P1 (interactive), P2 (background). Map priority->acceptable GPU families.
- Cost Shepherd computes a composite score: score = w_latency*affinity - w_cost*(expected_cost_multiplier)*eviction_risk_penalty. Selects top-ranked GPU family available in target region.

3) Spot evictions and predictive hedging:
- Use historical spot eviction metric per region/sku + real-time cloud market telemetry to compute eviction risk (0-1).
- If eviction risk * expected recovery_time_cost > budget_headroom impact, prefer on-demand or replicated allocations (hedged slots) for that request.
- For high-importance requests we may allocate a tiny hedged on-demand reservation for the next N tokens and continue on spot; the runtime supports seamless variant switch on eviction.

4) Model fallback variants:
- Implement automatic model-family fallbacks: primary (full fp16 H100 model), variant A (int8 A100-quantized), variant B (smaller distilled model).
- Fallback policy is prioritized: only fallback when soft-cap threshold reached OR predicted tail-cost vs. SLO indicates better overall application utility.
- Record quality delta (from offline evals) and expose per-tenant tradeoff logs for PM/Customer review.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit per-decision event: {tenant, request_id, timestamp, chosen_region, chosen_gpu_family, predicted_cost, actual_cost, eviction_risk, budget_window_usage, fallback_applied, model_variant}. (Events streamed to telemetry pipeline).
- Add console dashboard: Budget pulse (usage vs thresholds), Recent enforced fallbacks, Eviction risk heatmap, Per-tenant cost vs SLO tradeoffs.

API/Config:
- New routing policy config for tenants: {budget_window, soft_threshold, hard_threshold, priority_mapping, gpu_preference_overrides, allowed_model_variants, fallback_rules}.
- Admin API to temporarily lift hard caps for support or to pin routing to specific regions/GPU classes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests validating budget accounting and reservation lifecycle.
- E2E test simulating spot eviction and verifying hedged-on-demand fallback without request failure.
- Benchmark: <5% SLO violation increase for top-tier tenants under soft-cap triggering; cost reduction target of 12% vs naive on-demand baseline for low-priority traffic.
- Console shows per-tenant decision logs and a test tenant demonstrates fallback sequence.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement heuristics + unit tests behind feature flag. (1 sprint)
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for internal test tenants, collect telemetry, tune weights. (2 sprints)
- Phase 3 (gradual tenant opt-in): expose tenant config in Console + soft launch for select customers.
- Phase 4: GA; document in runbooks and SLO playbooks.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should soft caps be for multi-tenant noisy neighbors? Proposal: make soft thresholds tenant-configurable with conservative default (85%).
- Should hedging (allocating on-demand fallback slots) be charged immediately or only on eviction? Proposal: only charge hedged on-demand when consumed; reservation cost tracked as potential liability.
- Quantization vs SLO: automated fallback requires per-tenant quality guards. We will integrate Redwood Optimize eval scores to gate automatic fallbacks for flagged customers.

Related artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Cost+Shepherd+Design
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
- Telemetry schema: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/telemetry/schema#cost-shepherd

Implementation notes:
- Routing decisions live in the router service; budget ledger in the tenant billing service exposed via low-latency gRPC.
- Use token cost estimator library (existing) and add GPU-multiplier tables per cloud SKU.
- Add feature flag gating (FF: cost_shepherd_v1) and runtime knobs for w_latency/w_cost weights.
